Background (from the session that started this one):
Kenneth (JusPrin, a fork of OrcaSlicer whose built-in AI agent chats about the project) wants prompt testing to stop depending on paid per-token API models. In a 2026-10-19 session we tested the file-loaded skill a different way: we recorded the exact requests the app sends (pointing JUSPRIN_OPENAI_ENDPOINT at a local recorder), and had fresh Opus 5.5 subagents in a Claude Code session answer them. That surfaced prompt-caused problems clearly. Kenneth's reasoning: production users will often use stronger models than DeepSeek V4 Flash, testing strong models over the API is too expensive to do routinely, and the coding subscription already pays for a strong model. Those subagents read a Markdown dump and could not make real tool calls, and they knew they were being tested. Headless `claude -p` with a custom system prompt and an MCP stub fixes most of that and can be driven from the existing Python runner.

Task:
Add a backend to tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py (and, if it shares the code, tests/printer_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py) that answers each recorded step with the locally installed Claude Code CLI in headless mode, instead of POSTing to OpenRouter (model) and OpenAI (judge). The goal is prompt iteration that bills the developer's Claude subscription, not API usage.

What exists: the runner replays requests recorded from the app (tests/project_prompt/requests.json, recorded by the shell harness). It sends each one to deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash on OpenRouter (MODEL, ENDPOINT, post()). It answers read-only tool calls from recorded results, at most three reads (recorded_answer, answers_for, run_once, MAX_READS). It judges the step with JUDGE_MODEL gpt-5.5 over the OpenAI API (judge(), judge_response()). The README in tests/project_prompt explains the step rules. test_steps.py checks them offline.

Design to implement, keeping all of today's step rules:
- New flag, e.g. `--backend claude-cli [--claude-model opus]`. The default stays as today.
- Per run: `claude -p --model <m> --system-prompt <the request's instructions> --tools "" --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config <generated json> --output-format stream-json --no-session-persistence`. The 2.1.283 CLI has all of these flags; verify the exact behaviour, and whether `--bare` keeps subscription auth.
- Real tool calling through a small stdio MCP stub server written in Python under tests/project_prompt/. It exposes the 28 tools from project_tools.json with their real schemas. Read-only calls are answered with today's recorded answers. The first change call is recorded as the step and ends the run, exactly as today. Parse which tool calls happened from the stream-json output.
- Render the recorded input items (user text parts, the <workspace> block, images if the CLI accepts image input in stream-json, and the app's developer-role notes) into the prompt. Claude has no developer role, so render those notes as clearly labelled app text and say so in the README. This is the same fidelity question the README already describes for DeepSeek hosts.
- Judge on the subscription too (`claude -p --json-schema` for a yes/no verdict), behind its own flag, because changing the judge resets the baselines (see the "confirmed results become the baseline" convention in the README/handoffs).
- Run several cases in parallel with a small cap, so the subscription's rate limits aren't hit all at once.
- README: when to use which backend. Opus on the subscription measures what the prompt itself causes, and is cheap to iterate with. The app's default model is gpt-5.4-mini (OpenAIResponsesAgent.hpp), which scored about like DeepSeek in the README's model table. So a strong model can paper over ambiguities a weaker one trips on, and a small paid run on the app's default stays the pre-release check.

Constraints:
- Never run live paid API batches without Kenneth approving a specific batch (tests/project_prompt/README.md).
- Show the subscription runs to Kenneth before running many: start with one case, end to end.
- Don't commit handoff or working docs.

Done = `--backend claude-cli` runs one recorded case end to end with real MCP tool calls answered from recordings and a verdict; test_steps.py still passes; the README documents it. Report the per-case wall-clock time.

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""One step of the project chat against the live model, without the app.
3	
4	The project chat's assistant is a system prompt (projectInstructions.ts), the
5	project tools and the chat. Each case here is one point in a project chat,
6	recorded from the real app, and the model's next step there, a tool call or a
7	reply, checked against one sentence of the prompt. A response may hold
8	several calls, and every one is judged: a change among them is the outcome
9	and ends the run, whatever came before it. A response of reads the case does
10	not decide on is answered, each read with the result the app gave for it at
11	the same point (recorded beside the request), and the model asked again, at
12	most MAX_READS times; nothing else is ever answered.
13	
14	What the app sends, reproduced here:
15	  - instructions: rendered from projectInstructions.ts by
16	    tests/printer_prompt/render_prompt.mjs, so an edit to the prompt is tested
17	    without building anything;
18	  - tools: project_tools.json, the app's own tool list for the project chat
19	    (test_openai_responses_agent.cpp fails if it drifts from the registry);
20	  - input: everything else, as the app built it (requests.json). The shell
21	    harness's --project-prompt-requests mode plays script.json through the
22	    real app, with the model's outputs scripted and every tool run for real,
23	    and keeps the request at each point a case observes: the earlier turns as
24	    the app replays them, this turn's message with the workspace context, and
25	    this turn's calls with their live results. At the same point it calls
26	    the reads script.json's "answers" lists (workspace_inspect, slice_report,
27	    printer_list, object_analyze for each object, settings_get of every
28	    setting of the print, the first object, the filament and the printer,
29	    the filament's and printer's names asked under the print scope, a
30	    hand-kept list of other slicers' names, and settings_search for common
31	    queries) and keeps
32	    their results: those are the only answers a read can get.
33	The app streams its requests; this script does not. Nothing else differs,
34	except which model answers them.
35	
36	Usage:
37	  OPENROUTER_API_KEY=... OPENAI_API_KEY=... tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py
38	      [--runs N] [--must-pass N] [--case NAME] [--jobs 5] [--verbose] [--prompt-rev REV]
39	      [--model NAME [--endpoint URL] [--key-env NAME] [--provider HOST]...]
40	  tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py --render-only [--case NAME] [--runs N] [--prompt-rev REV]
41	
42	--render-only sends nothing: it prints each case's full request body, one JSON
43	object per line, and on stderr the size of each and of the batch.
44	
45	Prompt changes are evaluated on DeepSeek V4 Flash through OpenRouter, pinned to
46	the hosts tests/printer_prompt names (MODEL, PROVIDERS), and on nothing else.
47	The judge stays on OpenAI (OPENAI_API_KEY) whichever model answers.
48	
49	Without --runs, the cases run share RUN_BUDGET runs: 3 each for 22 cases,
50	never more than MAX_RUNS for one case.
51	
52	Exit code 0 when every case passes at least --must-pass of its runs (default:
53	all of them), 1 otherwise. Needs python3 and node, and the page's npm install
54	(src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/node_modules) for esbuild.

163	    """A yes or no about the conversation's last reply, from a stronger model,
164	    for what no string test can check. Returns (yes, why)."""
165	    schema = {"type": "object", "additionalProperties": False, "required": ["answer", "why"],
166	              "properties": {"answer": {"type": "string", "enum": ["yes", "no"]}, "why": {"type": "string"}}}
167	    response = post({"model": JUDGE_MODEL, "store": False,

173	    count(response.get("usage"), judge=True)
174	    text = "".join(output_text(item) for item in response.get("output", []) if item.get("type") == "message")

179	def readable(item, limit=1500):
180	    """One input item as a line of the judge's transcript."""
181	    if item.get("type") == "function_call":
182	        return f"tool call: {item['name']} {item['arguments']}"
183	    if item.get("type") == "function_call_output":

186	    if "role" not in item:

190	    # <print_issue> blocks, attachments) are separate in the request; keep
191	    # them apart here too.
192	    text = content if isinstance(content, str) else "\n\n".join(part["text"] for part in content or [] if "text" in part)

198	    for item in reversed(request["body"]["input"]):

204	class Step:
205	    """What the model did with the request: its reply, or the tool call that
206	    stands for its calls. A response may hold several calls, and the app runs
207	    every one, so a change among them is the step whatever came before it
208	    (the first change, if several); a response of reads is the first read,
209	    and each_read() gives a step for every read. Every call is in the report."""
210	
211	    def __init__(self, output, index=None):
212	        self.output = output
213	        self.calls = [item for item in output if item.get("type") == "function_call"]
214	        self.reply = "".join(output_text(item) for item in output if item.get("type") == "message").strip()
215	        if index is None:
216	            index = next((i for i, item in enumerate(self.calls) if item.get("name") not in READS), 0)
217	        self.index = index
218	        call = self.calls[index] if self.calls else None
219	        self.tool = call["name"] if call else None
220	        self.call_id = call.get("call_id") if call else None
221	        self.arguments = self.parsed(call) if call else {}
222	        self.problem = self.invalid() if call else ""
223	
224	    @staticmethod
225	    def parsed(call):
226	        try:
227	            return json.loads(call.get("arguments") or "{}")
228	        except json.JSONDecodeError:
229	            return {"(unreadable)": call.get("arguments")}
230	
231	    def each_read(self):
232	        """A step for every call of a response with no change in it, in the
233	        order the model wrote them."""
234	        return [Step(self.output, index) for index in range(len(self.calls))]

236	    def invalid(self):
237	        """Arguments the registry would refuse, as far as the schema says. The
238	        refusal is not this suite's to test; it is reported beside the call."""
239	        schema = next((tool["parameters"] for tool in TOOLS if tool["name"] == self.tool), None)
240	        if schema is None:
241	            return "unknown tool"
242	        missing = [name for name in schema.get("required", []) if name not in self.arguments]
243	        extra = [name for name in self.arguments if name not in schema.get("properties", {})]
244	        return f"invalid arguments: missing {missing}, unexpected {extra}" if missing or extra else ""

246	    def keys(self):
247	        """The settings a settings call names."""
248	        return set(self.arguments.get("keys") or []) | set(self.arguments.get("changes") or {})

251	        return self.tool is not None and self.tool not in READS
252	
253	    def reads(self):

257	        if not self.tool:

260	        others = [f"{call['name']} {json.dumps(self.parsed(call), ensure_ascii=False)}"

267	# Each case names its request in requests.json and, in its docstring, the
268	# sentence of projectInstructions.ts it tests (line numbers at 6b4b8b6188).
269	# check() returns PASS, FAIL, UNOBSERVED or CONTINUE with a detail. CONTINUE
270	# is a read the case does not decide on: when it decides on none of a
271	# response's reads, the runner answers them all from the recording and asks
272	# again. UNOBSERVED is a step the case can say nothing about, or a read with

276	class Case:
277	    def __init__(self, request, log):
278	        self.request, self.log = request, log
279	
280	    def judged(self, step, question):
281	        yes, why = judge(self.log + ["assistant: " + step.reply], question)
282	        return yes, why
283	
284	    def reply_or_read(self, step):
285	        """A reply passes, a change fails, a read is answered."""
286	        if step.changes():
287	            return FAIL, "CHANGED: " + str(step)
288	        return (CONTINUE if step.tool else PASS), str(step)
289	
290	    def judged_reply(self, step, question, claim):
291	        """For cases about what a reply says: a change fails, a read is
292	        answered, and the reply fails when the judge says yes."""
293	        if step.tool:
294	            return (FAIL if step.changes() else CONTINUE), str(step)
295	        yes, why = self.judged(step, question)
296	        return (FAIL, claim + why) if yes else (PASS, str(step))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""A fake Anthropic Messages endpoint: records every request body and answers
with scripted responses (a JSON list of content-block lists, one per request).
Usage: fake_anthropic.py PORT RECORD_DIR SCRIPT_JSON"""
import http.server, json, sys, os, itertools, threading

PORT, RECORD, SCRIPT = int(sys.argv[1]), sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
os.makedirs(RECORD, exist_ok=True)
counter = itertools.count(1)
lock = threading.Lock()


class Handler(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def log_message(self, *a):
        sys.stderr.write("%s %s\n" % (self.command, self.path))

    def do_GET(self):
        self.send_response(404); self.end_headers()

    def do_HEAD(self):
        self.send_response(200); self.end_headers()

    def do_POST(self):
        body = self.rfile.read(int(self.headers.get("content-length", 0)))
        if not self.path.startswith("/v1/messages") or "count_tokens" in self.path:
            self.send_response(404); self.end_headers(); return
        with lock:
            n = next(counter)
            open(os.path.join(RECORD, f"req{n}.json"), "wb").write(body)
            open(os.path.join(RECORD, f"req{n}.headers"), "w").write(str(dict(self.headers)))
            script = json.load(open(SCRIPT))
        req = json.loads(body)
        blocks = script[min(n - 1, len(script) - 1)]
        if not req.get("stream"):
            # e.g. a side query: answer plain text
            self.send_response(200); self.send_header("content-type", "application/json"); self.end_headers()
            self.wfile.write(json.dumps({"id": f"msg_{n}", "type": "message", "role": "assistant", "model": req["model"],
                                         "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "ok"}], "stop_reason": "end_turn",
                                         "usage": {"input_tokens": 1, "output_tokens": 1}}).encode()); return
        self.send_response(200); self.send_header("content-type", "text/event-stream"); self.end_headers()

        def ev(name, data):
            self.wfile.write(f"event: {name}\ndata: {json.dumps(data)}\n\n".encode()); self.wfile.flush()
        ev("message_start", {"type": "message_start", "message": {"id": f"msg_{n}", "type": "message", "role": "assistant",
            "model": req["model"], "content": [], "stop_reason": None, "usage": {"input_tokens": 10, "output_tokens": 1}}})
        stop = "end_turn"
        for i, b in enumerate(blocks):
            if b["type"] == "text":
                ev("content_block_start", {"type": "content_block_start", "index": i, "content_block": {"type": "text", "text": ""}})
                ev("content_block_delta", {"type": "content_block_delta", "index": i, "delta": {"type": "text_delta", "text": b["text"]}})
            else:
                stop = "tool_use"
                ev("content_block_start", {"type": "content_block_start", "index": i, "content_block":
                    {"type": "tool_use", "id": f"toolu_{n}_{i}", "name": b["name"], "input": {}}})
                ev("content_block_delta", {"type": "content_block_delta", "index": i, "delta":
                    {"type": "input_json_delta", "partial_json": json.dumps(b["input"])}})
            ev("content_block_stop", {"type": "content_block_stop", "index": i})
        ev("message_delta", {"type": "message_delta", "delta": {"stop_reason": stop, "stop_sequence": None},
                             "usage": {"output_tokens": 5}})
        ev("message_stop", {"type": "message_stop"})


http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", PORT), Handler).serve_forever()

summaries, PR descriptions — is written for a generalist full-stack
engineer who did NOT see this session.

## Format contract
- Every summary or status update opens with 2–3 sentences that a
  cold reader can understand. Details after.

## The one rule
- No noun phrase that needs this session's context to resolve.
  Test each sentence: does it parse for someone reading only this
  message? If not, expand it — name the thing, don't point at it.
- Define any unavoidable domain term inline, in one clause, on
  first use.

## Showing output
- When asked to show a diff, file, or command output: reproduce it
  in the reply text. Never say "as shown" or "that's the whole X"
  while pointing at a tool result.

"""The claude-cli backend of run_prompt_tests.py: one recorded step answered by
the locally installed Claude Code CLI in headless mode, on the developer's
Claude subscription instead of a paid API key.

How a recorded request reaches the model:
  - instructions: the CLI's --system-prompt. The CLI puts two lines of its own
    before it (a billing header and "You are a Claude agent, built on
    Anthropic's Claude Agent SDK.") and adds a short "# Environment" block
    after the first message (working directory, platform, date, model name).
  - tools: the stub MCP server (claude_mcp_stub.py) serves the case's tools
    with their real descriptions and schemas. The model sees each under the
    CLI's MCP name, mcp__jusprin__<name>; the runner strips the prefix.
  - input: everything before the request's last turn is written as a
    session file the CLI resumes (--resume <file>), so earlier messages,
    calls and results reach the model as real turns, tool calls and tool
    results. The last turn's message (the person's words, the <workspace>
    block, the plate's picture) goes in on stdin as one stream-json user
    message. A developer-role item becomes a user text block wrapped in
    <developer_message> tags: the Messages API has no developer role.
  - a point recorded mid-turn (the request ends on a tool result) resumes a
    session whose last call is marked deferred: the CLI runs that call
    through the stub, which returns the recorded result (and the app's
    developer notes after it, as further text blocks of the same result),
    and then asks the model, adding its own "Continue from where you left
    off." after the result.
Every later call goes through the stub to the runner, which answers it with
answer() or ends the run by closing the process.

Nothing from the developer's own Claude Code setup reaches the model:
--setting-sources "" (no settings, hooks or output style), no CLAUDE.md and no
auto-memory (environment), --disable-slash-commands (no skills),
--strict-mcp-config (only the stub), --tools "" (no built-in tools), a
minimal environment, and an empty working directory."""

import json
import os
import pathlib
import queue
import shutil
import signal
import socket
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import threading
import time
import uuid

HERE = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
STUB = HERE / "claude_mcp_stub.py"
SERVER = "jusprin"
PREFIX = f"mcp__{SERVER}__"
# The tool the CLI adds for --json-schema.
STRUCTURED_OUTPUT = "StructuredOutput"
# For an offline check against a fake Messages endpoint: its URL. The CLI is
# then given a dummy API key instead of the subscription's login.
TEST_ENDPOINT_ENV = "JUSPRIN_CLAUDE_CLI_TEST_ENDPOINT"
RUN_TIMEOUT = 900  # seconds for one run, every response included


def environment():
    """A minimal environment: the CLI reads the subscription's login from the
    user's keychain or config, never an API key or a parent session's."""
    env = {key: os.environ[key] for key in ("HOME", "USER", "LOGNAME", "PATH", "LANG", "TMPDIR", "SHELL", "TERM")
           if key in os.environ}
    env.update({"CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_MDS": "1", "CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY": "1",
                "DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER": "1", "MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT": str(RUN_TIMEOUT * 1000)})
    if os.environ.get(TEST_ENDPOINT_ENV):
        env.update({"ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL": os.environ[TEST_ENDPOINT_ENV], "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY": "sk-fake-for-tests"})
    return env


def isolation_args(cwd):
    return ["--tools", "", "--strict-mcp-config", "--setting-sources", "", "--disable-slash-commands",
            "--no-session-persistence"]


def check_auth(init):
    """Refuses a run billed to anything but the subscription's login."""
    source = init.get("apiKeySource")
    if source != "none" and not os.environ.get(TEST_ENDPOINT_ENV):
        raise RuntimeError(f"the Claude CLI would bill {source}, not the subscription; unset it or log in with "
                           "`claude auth login`")


def find_claude():
    claude = shutil.which("claude")
    if claude is None:
        sys.exit("the claude-cli backend needs the Claude Code CLI (`claude`) on PATH")
    return claude


# --- The recorded request as a session ----------------------------------------


def developer_block(text):
    return {"type": "text", "text": f"<developer_message>\n{text}\n</developer_message>"}


def user_blocks(item):
    """A user or developer item of the Responses API as Messages content."""
    if item["role"] == "developer":
        content = item["content"]
        return [developer_block(content if isinstance(content, str) else
                                "\n\n".join(part.get("text", "") for part in content))]
    content = item["content"]
    if isinstance(content, str):
        return [{"type": "text", "text": content}]
    blocks = []
    for part in content:
        if part["type"] == "input_text":
            blocks.append({"type": "text", "text": part["text"]})
        elif part["type"] == "input_image":
            header, data = part["image_url"].split(",", 1)  # data:image/png;base64,...
            blocks.append({"type": "image", "source": {"type": "base64", "media_type": header[5:].split(";")[0],
                                                       "data": data}})
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"unsupported input part {part['type']}")
    return blocks


def messages(items):
    """Responses API input items as Messages API messages, consecutive items
    of one role in one message."""
    out = []

    def push(role, blocks):
        if out and out[-1]["role"] == role:
            out[-1]["content"] += blocks
        else:
            out.append({"role": role, "content": list(blocks)})

    for item in items:
        kind = item.get("type")
        if kind == "function_call":
            push("assistant", [{"type": "tool_use", "id": item["call_id"], "name": PREFIX + item["name"],
                                "input": json.loads(item.get("arguments") or "{}")}])
        elif kind == "function_call_output":
            push("user", [{"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": item["call_id"], "content": item["output"]}])
        elif item.get("role") in ("user", "developer"):
            push("user", user_blocks(item))
        elif item.get("role") == "assistant":
            content = item["content"]
            text = content if isinstance(content, str) else "".join(part.get("text", "") for part in content)
            push("assistant", [{"type": "text", "text": text}])
        elif kind == "reasoning":
            continue
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"unsupported input item {kind or item.get('role')}")
    return out


def split(items):
    """(history, last message, deferred call) for a recorded request.
    A request that ends on the person's message (with the app's notes after
    it): the history is everything before that message. One that ends
    mid-turn on a tool result: the history runs to the last call, which is
    deferred, and its result and the notes after it are the deferred answer."""
    end = len(items)
    while end and items[end - 1].get("role") == "developer":
        end -= 1
    if end and items[end - 1].get("type") == "function_call_output":
        output, call = items[end - 1], items[end - 2]
        if call.get("type") != "function_call" or call["call_id"] != output["call_id"] or \
                items[end - 3].get("type") == "function_call":
            raise ValueError("a mid-turn point must end on one call and its result")
        notes = [block["text"] for item in items[end:] for block in user_blocks(item)]
        return items[:end - 1], None, (call, [output["output"]] + notes)
    start = end
    while start and items[start - 1].get("role") in ("user", "developer"):
        start -= 1
    return items[:start], items[start:], None


def session_file(path, history, cwd, deferred):
    """A session the CLI can resume: the history as a chain of entries, and
    the deferred call's marker when the point is mid-turn."""
    session, parent, lines = str(uuid.uuid4()), None, []

    def add(kind, **fields):
        nonlocal parent
        entry = {"parentUuid": parent, "isSidechain": False, "userType": "external", "cwd": str(cwd),
                 "sessionId": session, "version": "2.1.283", "type": kind, "uuid": str(uuid.uuid4()),
                 "timestamp": "2026-10-19T00:00:00.000Z", **fields}
        lines.append(json.dumps(entry, ensure_ascii=False))
        parent = entry["uuid"]

    for index, message in enumerate(messages(history)):
        if message["role"] == "assistant":
            add("assistant", message={"id": f"msg_recorded_{index}", "type": "message", "role": "assistant",
                                      "model": "recorded", "content": message["content"],
                                      "stop_reason": "tool_use" if message["content"][-1]["type"] == "tool_use"
                                      else "end_turn", "usage": {"input_tokens": 0, "output_tokens": 0}})
        else:
            add("user", message=message)
    if deferred:
        call = deferred[0]
        add("attachment", attachment={"type": "hook_deferred_tool", "toolUseID": call["call_id"],
                                      "toolName": PREFIX + call["name"],
                                      "toolInput": json.loads(call.get("arguments") or "{}"),
                                      "hookName": "settings", "hookEvent": "PreToolUse", "permissionMode": "default"})
    path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")


def key(name, arguments):
    return name + " " + json.dumps(arguments, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))


# --- One run ------------------------------------------------------------------


class Run:
    """The CLI answering one recorded request, response by response.
    next_response() returns the model's next response as Responses API
    output items; answer() gives the results of its calls, and the CLI asks
    the model again. close() ends it, whatever it is doing."""

    def __init__(self, instructions, tools, items, model, effort, keep=None):
        self.directory = pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="jp-cli-", dir="/tmp"))  # a short socket path
        self.keep = keep
        self.events = queue.Queue()
        self.answers, self.answers_lock = {}, threading.Condition()
        self.usage = []
        self.started = time.monotonic()
        cwd = self.directory / "cwd"
        cwd.mkdir()
        (self.directory / "tools.json").write_text(json.dumps(tools), encoding="utf-8")
        self.socket_path = str(self.directory / "s")
        (self.directory / "mcp.json").write_text(json.dumps({"mcpServers": {SERVER: {
            "command": sys.executable, "args": [str(STUB), str(self.directory / "tools.json"), self.socket_path]}}}))
        history, last, deferred = split(items)
        if deferred:
            self.provide([(deferred[0]["name"], json.loads(deferred[0].get("arguments") or "{}"), deferred[1])])
        self.listener = socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
        self.listener.bind(self.socket_path)
        self.listener.listen()
        threading.Thread(target=self.serve, daemon=True).start()

        command = [find_claude(), "-p", "--model", model, "--effort", effort, "--system-prompt", instructions,
                   "--mcp-config", str(self.directory / "mcp.json"), "--allowedTools", f"mcp__{SERVER}",
                   "--output-format", "stream-json", "--verbose", "--include-partial-messages"] + isolation_args(cwd)
        if history or deferred:
            session = self.directory / "session.jsonl"
            session_file(session, history, cwd, deferred)
            command += ["--resume", str(session)]
        stdin = None
        if last:
            command += ["--input-format", "stream-json"]
            stdin = json.dumps({"type": "user", "message": {"role": "user", "content": messages(last)[0]["content"]}},
                               ensure_ascii=False) + "\n"
        self.log = open(self.directory / "stream.jsonl", "w", encoding="utf-8")
        self.process = subprocess.Popen(command, cwd=cwd, env=environment(), stdin=subprocess.PIPE,
                                        stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=open(self.directory / "stderr.txt", "w"),
                                        encoding="utf-8", start_new_session=True)
        threading.Thread(target=self.read, daemon=True).start()
        if stdin:
            self.process.stdin.write(stdin)
        self.process.stdin.close()

    # The stub's calls, each on its own connection.
    def serve(self):
        while True:
            try:
                connection, _ = self.listener.accept()
            except OSError:
                return
            threading.Thread(target=self.handle, args=(connection,), daemon=True).start()

    def handle(self, connection):
        with connection:
            call = json.loads(connection.makefile("r", encoding="utf-8").readline())
            wanted = key(call["name"], call["arguments"])
            with self.answers_lock:
                while not self.answers.get(wanted):
                    self.answers_lock.wait()
                output = self.answers[wanted].pop(0)
            connection.sendall((json.dumps({"output": output}) + "\n").encode())

    def provide(self, answers):
        with self.answers_lock:
            for name, arguments, output in answers:
                self.answers.setdefault(key(name, arguments), []).append(output)
            self.answers_lock.notify_all()

    def read(self):
        for line in self.process.stdout:
            self.log.write(line)
            try:
                self.events.put(json.loads(line))
            except json.JSONDecodeError:
                continue
        self.events.put(None)

    def next_response(self):
        blocks, usage = [], {}
        while True:
            remaining = RUN_TIMEOUT - (time.monotonic() - self.started)
            try:
                event = self.events.get(timeout=max(remaining, 0.1))
            except queue.Empty:
                raise RuntimeError(f"no response from the Claude CLI in {RUN_TIMEOUT} s")
            if event is None:
                raise RuntimeError("the Claude CLI exited without a response: " + self.stderr_tail())
            kind = event.get("type")
            if kind == "system" and event.get("subtype") == "init":
                check_auth(event)
                if not any(server["name"] == SERVER and server["status"] == "connected"
                           for server in event.get("mcp_servers", [])):
                    raise RuntimeError(f"the tool stub did not connect: {event.get('mcp_servers')}")
            elif kind == "assistant" and not event.get("parent_tool_use_id"):
                blocks += event["message"]["content"]
            elif kind == "stream_event":
                raw = event["event"]
                if raw["type"] == "message_start":
                    usage = dict(raw["message"].get("usage") or {})
                elif raw["type"] == "message_delta":
                    usage["output_tokens"] = (raw.get("usage") or {}).get("output_tokens", 0)
                elif raw["type"] == "message_stop":
                    self.usage.append(usage)
                    return output_items(blocks), usage
            elif kind == "result":
                if event.get("is_error"):
                    raise RuntimeError("the Claude CLI failed: " + str(event.get("result"))[:500])
                raise RuntimeError("the Claude CLI finished without a response")

    def answer(self, calls, results):
        self.provide([(call["name"], json.loads(call.get("arguments") or "{}"), result)
                      for call, result in zip(calls, results)])

    def stderr_tail(self):
        try:
            return (self.directory / "stderr.txt").read_text(errors="replace")[-500:]
        except OSError:
            return ""

    def close(self):
        if self.process.poll() is None:
            try:
                os.killpg(self.process.pid, signal.SIGTERM)
                self.process.wait(timeout=10)
            except (ProcessLookupError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
                try:
                    os.killpg(self.process.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
                except ProcessLookupError:
                    pass
        self.listener.close()
        self.log.close()
        if self.keep:
            target = pathlib.Path(self.keep) / self.directory.name
            shutil.copytree(self.directory, target, ignore=shutil.ignore_patterns("s"))
        shutil.rmtree(self.directory, ignore_errors=True)

    def __enter__(self):
        return self

    def __exit__(self, *_):
        self.close()


def output_items(blocks):
    """The CLI's content blocks as the Responses API output items Step reads.
    Thinking blocks are the model's own and are left out, as reasoning items
    are."""
    items = []
    for block in blocks:

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The claude-cli backend against a fake Messages endpoint: what the model
would receive, and the step rules through real MCP calls. Runs the installed
Claude Code CLI with a dummy API key aimed at a local server, so it needs no
login, sends nothing anywhere and costs nothing. Skipped when `claude` is not
on PATH. Run it after a CLI update: the resumed session is the CLI's own
internal format.

Usage: python3 tests/project_prompt/test_claude_cli.py
"""

import http.server
import importlib.util
import json
import os
import pathlib
import shutil
import threading
import unittest

HERE = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("run_prompt_tests", HERE / "run_prompt_tests.py")
runner = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(runner)
cli = runner.claude_cli


class FakeMessages:
    """Answers each streamed request with the next scripted response (a list
    of content blocks) and keeps every request body."""

    def __init__(self, *responses):
        self.responses, self.bodies = list(responses), []
        fake = self

        class Handler(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
            def log_message(self, *_):
                pass

            def do_HEAD(self):
                self.send_response(200)
                self.end_headers()

            def do_POST(self):
                body = json.loads(self.rfile.read(int(self.headers.get("content-length", 0))))
                if not self.path.startswith("/v1/messages") or "count_tokens" in self.path or not body.get("stream"):
                    self.send_response(404)
                    self.end_headers()
                    return
                fake.bodies.append(body)
                blocks = fake.responses.pop(0) if fake.responses else [{"type": "text", "text": "(nothing scripted)"}]
                self.send_response(200)
                self.send_header("content-type", "text/event-stream")
                self.end_headers()

                def event(data):
                    self.wfile.write(f"event: {data['type']}\ndata: {json.dumps(data)}\n\n".encode())

                event({"type": "message_start", "message": {"id": f"msg_{len(fake.bodies)}", "type": "message",
                       "role": "assistant", "model": body["model"], "content": [], "stop_reason": None,
                       "usage": {"input_tokens": 10, "output_tokens": 1}}})
                for index, block in enumerate(blocks):
                    if block["type"] == "text":
                        event({"type": "content_block_start", "index": index, "content_block": {"type": "text", "text": ""}})
                        event({"type": "content_block_delta", "index": index,
                               "delta": {"type": "text_delta", "text": block["text"]}})
                    else:
                        event({"type": "content_block_start", "index": index, "content_block":
                               {"type": "tool_use", "id": f"toolu_{len(fake.bodies)}_{index}", "name": block["name"],
                                "input": {}}})
                        event({"type": "content_block_delta", "index": index,
                               "delta": {"type": "input_json_delta", "partial_json": json.dumps(block["input"])}})
                    event({"type": "content_block_stop", "index": index})
                stop = "tool_use" if any(block["type"] == "tool_use" for block in blocks) else "end_turn"
                event({"type": "message_delta", "delta": {"stop_reason": stop, "stop_sequence": None},
                       "usage": {"output_tokens": 5}})
                event({"type": "message_stop"})

        self.server = http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Handler)
        threading.Thread(target=self.server.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
        self.url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.server.server_address[1]}"

    def close(self):
        self.server.shutdown()


def tool(name, arguments):
    return {"type": "tool_use", "name": cli.PREFIX + name, "input": arguments}


def plain(value):
    """A request's content without the CLI's cache markers."""
    if isinstance(value, list):
        return [plain(item) for item in value]
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return {key: plain(item) for key, item in value.items() if key != "cache_control"}
    return value


def texts(body):
    for message in body["messages"]:
        content = message["content"]

## Running on the Claude subscription (`--backend claude-cli`)

`--backend claude-cli` answers every step with the locally installed Claude
Code CLI in headless mode (`claude -p`), billed to the developer's Claude
subscription instead of a per-token API key. `--judge claude-cli` moves the
judge there as well. Neither needs a key; both need the CLI logged in once
with `claude auth login`. The runner refuses to start a run the CLI would bill
to an API key (`apiKeySource` other than the login).

```bash
tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py --backend claude-cli --judge claude-cli --case advice-infill --runs 1
```

The model defaults to `claude-opus-5-5` at effort `medium`, both pinned so a
count moves only when the prompt does (`--claude-model`, `--claude-effort`,
`--claude-judge-model`). `--claude-keep DIR` keeps each run's session file,
tool list, MCP config and the CLI's event stream for reading afterwards.

### Which backend for what

- **Iterating on a prompt or skill: the subscription.** A strong model
  answering the app's real requests, with real tool calls, shows what the
  prompt itself causes: an ambiguous sentence, a rule two sections disagree
  on, a skill that invites the wrong call. It costs no API money, so it can
  be run as often as the subscription's usage limits allow. Those limits are
  shared with the developer's own Claude Code work; start with one case and
  keep `--jobs` small.
- **Before a release: a small paid run on the app's default model.** The app
  defaults to `gpt-5.4-mini` (`OpenAIResponsesAgent.hpp`), which scored about
  like DeepSeek V4 Flash in the printer suite's model table. A strong model
  can paper over an ambiguity a weaker one trips on, so a pass on Opus does
  not show the shipped default will pass. That run needs Kenneth's approval
  like every paid batch.
- **The baselines below** are DeepSeek V4 Flash with the OpenAI judge. A
  claude-cli count is never compared with them. Changing the judge changes
  what every judged case counts, so `--judge claude-cli` results start their
  own baseline, under the same "confirmed results become the baseline" rule.

### How a recorded request reaches the CLI

`claude_cli.py` turns each recorded request into a CLI run, and
`claude_mcp_stub.py` serves the tools:

- **System prompt**: the rendered prompt, as `--system-prompt`.
- **Tools**: the stub is a stdio MCP server with the case's tools (the 28 of
  `project_tools.json`, or the point's own list), with their real
  descriptions and schemas. Every call the model makes reaches the runner
  through it, and the step rules above apply unchanged: a read is answered
  with the recorded answer, a change ends the run (the runner stops the CLI;
  nothing is answered), a response of reads decides or is answered whole.
- **History**: the request's items before its last turn are written as a
  session file the CLI resumes (`--resume <file>`), so earlier messages,
  calls and results reach the model as its own turns, tool calls and tool
  results, not as a transcript. The last turn's message (the person's words,
  the `<workspace>` block, the plate's picture) goes in as one stream-json
  user message.
- **A point recorded mid-turn**, after a tool result (`after-preview`,
  `after-apply`, `after-slice`, `after-intent`, `direct-change-applied`,
  `direct-change-failed`, `first-person`, `slice-refused-by-tool`): the
  session ends on that turn's last call, marked as a deferred call. The CLI
  runs it through the stub, which returns the recorded result, and then asks
  the model.

Nothing from the developer's own Claude Code setup reaches the model: no
CLAUDE.md, auto-memory, settings, hooks, output style, skills, other MCP
servers or built-in tools, a minimal environment, and an empty temporary
working directory. `test_claude_cli.py` checks that, and the shapes above,
by running the installed CLI against a fake Messages endpoint on localhost
(no login, nothing sent; about 10 seconds). Run it after a CLI update: the
session file is the CLI's internal format, verified against 2.1.283.

What differs from the app's request, beyond the model:

- **Developer messages.** The Messages API has no developer role, so each of
  the app's developer items (its notes after a file-load report, the skills)
  is a user text block wrapped in `<developer_message>` tags. Hosts that
  drop or demote the developer role raise the same question for the API
  backend.
- **The CLI's own text.** Before the prompt, the CLI sends a billing header
  and "You are a Claude agent, built on Anthropic's Claude Agent SDK."; after
  the first message it adds a short environment note (the temporary working
  directory, platform, date and model name) and an empty system turn
  carrying the effort setting.
- **Tool names** carry the CLI's MCP prefix: the model sees
  `mcp__jusprin__settings_get`, while descriptions, which name other tools
  bare, are unchanged. The runner strips the prefix.
- **Mid-turn points**: after the deferred call's result, the CLI adds
  "Continue from where you left off." as a user message. The app's notes
  that follow the result there (the setup skill in `after-intent`, the
  slice-failed skill in `slice-refused-by-tool`) are further text blocks of
  that same tool result, since the CLI resumes no message after it.
- **Notes sent once** (a point's `once`) stay in the history after the
  first answered read; the app leaves them out of the turn's later requests.
- **Pictures** reach the model, unlike on the pinned DeepSeek hosts, so
  `model-opened-unnamed`, `model-imported-by-tool` and `model-opened-by-tool`
  can be measured here.

# Claude Code CLI as a prompt-test backend: findings (2026-10-19)

Branch `claude/claude-cli-backend`, commit ddc771948a (on jusprin-newui 170d1ae080, unmerged).

Verified against CLI 2.1.283 with a fake Messages endpoint (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL + dummy key), which shows the exact request the CLI sends:

- `--bare` cannot use the subscription: it reads only ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / apiKeyHelper. Not used.
- `--safe-mode` also disables `--mcp-config` servers. Not used.
- Without care the CLI injects the user's ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md (which holds a Sentry token), the output style and memory. Kept out with `--setting-sources ""`, CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_MDS=1, CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1, `--disable-slash-commands`, `--strict-mcp-config`, `--tools ""`, minimal env.
- Unavoidable: billing header + "You are a Claude agent, built on Anthropic's Claude Agent SDK." before --system-prompt; an "# Environment" system turn; an empty system turn carrying effort; MCP tool names prefixed `mcp__<server>__` (CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_MCP_NO_PREFIX has no effect on CLI-configured servers).
- MCP tools need `--allowedTools mcp__<server>` or every call is refused for permission.
- stream-json input accepts assistant messages but reorders them and drops tool results: unusable for history.
- `--resume /path/to/session.jsonl` replays a hand-written session faithfully. If it ends on a tool result, the CLI inserts an assistant "No response requested." before the new message. A session ending on a call marked with a `hook_deferred_tool` attachment resumes with no prompt: the CLI runs that call (only the last deferred one) and adds "Continue from where you left off."
- `--json-schema` works via a forced StructuredOutput tool; the answer is `structured_output` in the result event.
- Running `claude` from inside a Claude desktop session inherits that session's auth env and fails ("OAuth session expired"); the runner passes a minimal environment instead. On this Mac the standalone CLI login itself was expired (`claude auth status`: loggedIn false), so no subscription run has happened yet.
- Homebrew node is broken on this Mac (missing icu4c@78); use ~/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin/node for render_prompt.mjs.
